subject: physics
title: Energy Stores & Transfers - Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet the 8 stores and how energy moves between them.
meta_desc: KS3 Physics: foundations of energy stores and transfer pathways.
final_note: Energy mapped! You can name every store and how it moves.

concepts.def: Kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, etc.
Energy moved between stores mechanically, electrically, by heating or radiation.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Scientists list 8 energy stores:

Chemical - food, fuel, batteries.
Kinetic - anything moving.
Gravitational - anything lifted up.
Elastic - springs, rubber bands.
Thermal - hot objects.
Magnetic - magnets near magnetic stuff.
Electrostatic - charged things.
Nuclear - inside atoms.

Energy moves between stores via 4 pathways:

Mechanically - a force does work.
Electrically - current in a wire.
Heating - hot to cold.
Radiation - waves like light or sound.

Stores hold energy; pathways move it!

You eat a banana (chemical) and walk - chemical -> kinetic (mechanically).

A torch: chemical (battery) -> electrical pathway -> light + thermal stores.

A bonfire: chemical store of wood -> thermal store of air + light pathway.

options: kinetic store
gravitational store
chemical store
sound store

mcqs.q: Petrol stores energy in which form?
options: thermal
kinetic
chemical
gravitational

mcqs.q: Do all stars end their lives as supernovae?
options: Yes — every star eventually explodes.
Yes — but only after billions of years on Earth's scale.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
No — only sufficiently massive stars (above about 8 solar masses) explode as supernovae; lower-mass stars become white dwarfs.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: It is also longer, because both increase together.
It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
Yes — but only after billions of years on Earth's scale.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Chemical store”?
options: Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.
Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy in a moving object; faster and heavier objects have more.

options: Where energy is held until transferred — like kinetic, gravitational, chemical, thermal.
Energy in hotter objects; transferred when in contact with cooler ones.
Energy can't be made or destroyed, only transferred from store to store.
Energy in food, fuel and batteries; released by reactions.
